envelope.description: Settle the stale-catalog hazard and ship a standalone built-catalog loader

body.title: Settle the stale-catalog hazard and ship a standalone built-catalog loader
body.summary: Settle and implement the one genuinely open design decision, as an independently testable unit ahead of any update wiring: maintenance.update runs inside a CLI process holding the PRE-update CONFIG_CATALOG in its module graph, while `npm run build` at src/cli/services/maintenance.ts:106-112 rewrites out/ underneath it — so an in-process reconcile against the resident module is a no-op for exactly the shape change this Story targets, and is indistinguishable from 'already normalized'. Resolution (a) is chosen: load the freshly built catalog module via `await import()` of the build output and pass it as reconcileConfig's injectable `catalog` argument; on import rejection fall back to (b) — report only and defer the authoritative reconcile to the next daemon boot (landed in t9), never claiming a confident no-change against the stale in-memory catalog. Deliver this as a standalone helper `loadBuiltCatalog(): Promise<readonly ConfigOption[] | null>` in src/config that returns the freshly imported catalog or null on import rejection, with unit tests against a built-catalog fixture directory and a missing-output case. Record the decision and its rationale in a doc comment on the helper; the call-site wiring and its rationale comment land in t12.
acceptanceChecks: `loadBuiltCatalog` is exported from src/config, obtains the catalog via dynamic import of the build output, and never returns the statically imported src/cli/config-catalog.js binding
A missing or moved build output makes loadBuiltCatalog resolve to null rather than throwing, and this is unit-tested against both a valid built-catalog fixture directory and a missing-output case
The returned catalog is validated to be a non-empty array of catalog rows before being returned; a malformed module resolves to null
The chosen resolution (a with fallback b) and its rationale are documented in a doc comment on the helper
`npx tsx --test 'src/config/__tests__/*.test.ts'` passes with no new package dependency

tests.name: loadBuiltCatalog — returns the freshly imported catalog from a built-catalog fixture directory, not the statically imported src/cli binding
loadBuiltCatalog — missing/moved build output resolves to null without throwing
loadBuiltCatalog — malformed or empty catalog module resolves to null after the non-empty-array-of-rows validation
